punchline: Howard Hughes could fly record-breaking planes, but he couldn't let anyone else run his companies.
thirty_sec: Howard Hughes had it all: an inherited fortune, flying records, films, businesses. And because he was so talented and so rich, he could insist on controlling everything himself. He wouldn't delegate, overruled the people around him and obsessed over details. His businesses paid heavily for it. Ryan Holiday uses him to show that success asks for a shift, from doing everything yourself to building systems and trusting other people.
question: What's one task you've held onto because you're good at it, even though someone else could learn it?
